title: RFID Eyelet Tag — Grommet-Mount for Canvas & Leather
summary: RFID eyelet tags pair a reinforced metal grommet (stainless, brass or nickel-plated steel) with a UHF EPC Gen2v2 or HF ISO 15693 inlay laminated between two sealed substrate layers. The grommet anchors the tag bolt-through, rivet-through or lace-through onto canvas tarps, leather goods, textile bags, sail-makers' goods, technical apparel, soft luggage, outdoor-industrial covers and linen-pool items where a pull-through eyelet is already part of the host design — so the tag lives in the same hole the original eyelet would have used, with no new piercing of the host material.

items: Oval or round laminated patch 50-90 mm long × 20-40 mm wide, 1.2-1.8 mm thick, mass 2-4 g.
Central brass / nickel / stainless grommet Ø 5.0 / 6.35 / 8.0 mm (standard sailmaker / canvas sizes) set through the laminate.

items: UHF 860-960 MHz — ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2 ({chip:impinj-m730:name} / M750 / M830).
HF 13.56 MHz — ISO 15693 (I-CODE SLIX2) or ISO 14443 (NTAG 424 DNA) for tap-authentication variants.

brief.label: Substrate + eyelet mechanics
items: PVC + TPU laminate sandwich with RF-welded seam; reinforced patch ring around the grommet keeps the hole from tearing.
Grommet set with 500-800 N pull-out resistance per DIN 53351; antenna foil routed around the hole rather than through it.

Dimensional stability under AATCC 135; colour-fastness per ISO 105-C06 / ISO 105-X12 for the printed face of the patch.

-30 °C to +85 °C service; 500-hour QUV and 720-hour ISO 9227 salt-fog validated on the grommet-set edge.

ASTM D751 coated-fabric breaking-strength test profile for technical textile and tarp hosts.

HF tap — 0-40 mm against phone / POS / laundry-conveyor reader head.

sections.title: Why canvas, leather and textile assets demand a grommet-anchored tag
bullets: Soft-goods hosts — canvas tarps, leather luggage, sail-makers' products, uniforms, hospitality linen — do not present a rigid mounting face, so clip-on, cable-tie and screw-mount tag geometries either fall off in service or tear the host material.

The original pattern of the host usually already includes a reinforced eyelet for lashing, hanging or rope attachment. A grommet-mount RFID tag re-uses that same hole, keeping the tag inline with the existing piercing and minimising load concentration on the host.

Industrial laundry runs ISO 6330 wash cycles at 40-75 °C, pH 8-11 chemistry and 50-100 G tumble agitation for 200+ cycles across the service life; any label-glue bond will fail — grommet-anchored attachment is the only option that survives.
Marine and outdoor-industrial tarps see 500-1000 hours of UV, 720-hour salt-fog and mechanical abrasion; tags must be retained by physical grommet capture, not adhesive.
For leather-goods and luxury authentication, a grommet sewn under the lining provides tamper-evident attachment — the grommet cannot be removed without leaving a visible scar on the host leather.

sections.title: Sew-in, heat-seal, adhesive or grommet — why the eyelet wins on soft goods
bullets: Sew-in patches depend on thread integrity; a single thread failure pulls the tag off. Repair-audit rate in healthcare linen pools typically sits at 3-6 % per cycle for sewn tags.
Heat-seal patches bond to the host fabric through adhesive film; cycle life falls sharply above 75 °C wash or 80 °C ironing, and a failed bond cannot be re-applied in the field.
Adhesive stick-on tags fail on leather (surface oils), on technical fabric DWR finishes (low surface energy) and on canvas (rough weave). They are a poor choice for durable attached-tag applications.

Grommet-anchored eyelet tags put the retention load on a brass / stainless ring set through both the tag laminate and the host, with a 500-800 N DIN 53351 pull-out; the tag is retained for the service life of the host.
The eyelet path also carries the lashing rope, hanging cord, zip-tie or carabiner; the RFID tag does not add a new piercing to the host — it lives in the hole already there.

dataHighlight.heading: UHF portal-read accuracy at industrial-laundry inbound and outbound chutes
dataHighlight.text: Industrial laundries that move a full healthcare linen pool through UHF eyelet-tagged garments report inbound / outbound chute-portal read accuracy at ≥ 99.5 % per cart (50-100 items per pass), against 70-85 % barcode-scan accuracy and 85-95 % heat-seal-label accuracy over the same wash-cycle life, because the grommet-anchored tag physically cannot fall off during the 200+ cycle ISO 6330 service life.
dataHighlight.source: TRSA (Textile Rental Services Association) Clean Green certification guidance and UNIFORMPA market data summarised in the industry benchmark study on RFID in healthcare linen pools, 2023.

sections.title: How to roll out an RFID eyelet programme without compromising textile compliance
bullets: Size the grommet to the host: Ø 5.0 mm for light canvas / leather, Ø 6.35 mm for healthcare linen and standard soft-goods, Ø 8.0 mm for marine / outdoor tarps and heavy lashings — match the sailmaker eyelet size already in use on the host pattern.
Choose the substrate chemistry for the service envelope: PVC + TPU for industrial laundry; halogen-free TPU for sustainability-audited textile hosts; reinforced silicone on outdoor / marine hosts.
Lock the factory TID and permalock the EPC / NDEF payload after WMS / POS encode — an unlocked tag is the single biggest failure mode in brand-protection and healthcare-linen pilots.
Bring chemical-compliance artefacts into the supplier pack: REACH SVHC screen, RoHS 3 DoC, ZDHC MRSL and Higg Index entry for the tag as a durable-attached component.

Register the pool-tag in EPCIS 2.0 with a GRAI (reusable asset) identifier; consumer-facing trade items use SGTIN, while leather-goods authentication anchors carry NTAG 424 DNA SUN URLs under an NDEF permalock.

For healthcare linen, align with TRSA Hygienically Clean Healthcare certification and CDC Environmental Infection Control Guidelines G.VII (linen and laundry) so the tag programme is part of the HAI-prevention evidence pack.

items.label: Week 1 — host + grommet matrix
items.text: Cover every host SKU — linen, garment, tarp, leather good, harness bag — with a grommet size, substrate chemistry and chip choice; run a DIN 53351 pull-out + ISO 13934-1 tear sample on each.

items.label: Weeks 2-3 — laundry / outdoor validation
items.text: Cycle samples through 200+ ISO 6330 wash cycles at 40-75 °C plus 720-hour salt-fog and 500-hour QUV; confirm attachment-loss < 0.5 % per cycle and read-range drift < 10 %.

items.label: Weeks 4-6 — encoding workflow
items.text: Stand up the WMS / POS / laundry-pool encode bench that writes a locked EPC / NDEF, issues lock / permalock and commits an EPCIS commissioning event to ERP. Run a 100 % lock-rate check on the first 5,000 grommet tags.

items.label: Weeks 7-10 — portal + tunnel-wash rollout
items.text: Deploy UHF chute / tunnel-wash portals; tune antenna power so each cart of 50-100 items reads with < 0.5 % miss rate and zero cross-read into the adjacent cart. For brand-protection, align NTAG 424 DNA SUN URL format with the brand-protection backend.

items.label: Month 4+ — scale and audit
items.text: Sister-vertical playbooks include healthcare-linen and outdoor-canvas — each carries its own quarterly review pattern, refresh-window planning and supplier-vetting protocol. scale from pilot pool to 500,000 – 5,000,000 garments / tarps across multi-site laundries and rental fleets, with EPCIS event stream → ERP / rental-management / brand-protection analytics and a TRSA / Higg / ZDHC evidence pack on every quarter close.

sections.title: Inside the eyelet tag — a metal grommet through a sealed laminate
sections.intro: A soft-goods tag has one job that glue keeps failing at: staying attached. The eyelet tag solves it the way sailmakers solved it a century ago — a reinforced metal grommet set clean through the laminate and the host, so the tag hangs off the same hole the lashing already used. Everything else in the stack just protects the inlay long enough to matter. Its rigid-surface cousin is the [RFID hang tag](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-hang-tag/); the rest of the range lives in the [RFID tag catalogue](/products/rfid-tags/).

sections.title: Survives the wash, the sun and the salt that peel a glued-on tag
sections.intro: Adhesive is a fine way to attach a tag right up until the first hot wash, the first summer on a tarp, or the first season of sea spray — after which it is a fine way to lose one. The eyelet tag is retained by physical grommet capture, so the service envelope that strips a glued or sewn label barely registers. The small-format sibling for hard assets is the [RFID coin tag](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-coin-tag/); source-tagged garments carry the [RFID garment source tag](/products/rfid-labels/rfid-garment-source-tag/).

image.alt: Durability comparison: an RFID eyelet tag held by grommet capture passes three service stressors where a sewn, heat-seal or adhesive tag fails — 200+ ISO 6330 industrial-laundry wash cycles at 40-75 °C with under 0.5 % attachment-loss per cycle versus 3-6 % for sewn patches, 500 h QUV outdoor UV, and 720 h ISO 9227 salt-fog validated on a 316L stainless or brass grommet edge.

bullets: Industrial laundry — 200+ ISO 6330 wash cycles at 40-75 °C with under 0.5 % attachment-loss per cycle, against a 3-6 % per-cycle failure rate for sewn patches.
Heat-seal bonds degrade above 75 °C wash and 80 °C ironing and cannot be re-applied in the field; the metal grommet does not care.
Outdoor and marine — 500 h QUV on the UV-stabilised top-ply and 720 h ISO 9227 salt-fog validated on the grommet-set edge in 316L stainless or brass.
Adhesive fails on leather oils, low-surface-energy DWR fabric and rough-weave canvas; the grommet captures every one of those hosts through the same SKU.
Read range is unaffected because the inlay never leaves the host — UHF 1-3 m on canvas / leather and an HF 0-40 mm tap at the conveyor or POS reader head.

faq.question: Will the grommet damage the host fabric or leather?
faq.answer: No — the grommet lives in the same sailmaker / canvas eyelet size that the host pattern already uses for lashing rope, hanging cord or carabiner, so there is no new piercing of the host. The grommet ring distributes the pull-out load across 500-800 N per DIN 53351, well above the normal wearer / handling load, and the reinforced patch ring around the hole keeps the host from tearing at the edge.

faq.question: How many industrial-laundry cycles does an RFID eyelet tag actually survive?
faq.answer: The PVC + TPU laminate with an RF-welded seam and a brass or stainless grommet survives 200+ ISO 6330 cycles at 40-75 °C and pH 8-11 with less than 0.5 % per-cycle attachment-loss rate. The limiting factor is usually the host garment reaching end-of-life, not the tag — healthcare linen pools routinely report the tag outlasting 2-3 generations of sheets on the same grommet.

faq.question: Can the same SKU be used for both outdoor marine and indoor leather-goods authentication?
faq.answer: Yes — the grommet-mount SKU family spans both envelopes. The outdoor-marine variant uses a UV-stabilised TPU top-ply and a 720-hour salt-fog + 500-hour QUV validation; the leather-goods authentication variant uses an HF NTAG 424 DNA chip with a SUN message payload. Grommet alloy (brass or 316L stainless) is the other key spec to dial in for salt-water exposure.

faq.question: Which mount method should I use for each host material?
faq.answer: The RFID eyelet tag mounts four ways off one SKU, and the host material picks the method: sew-in or a lashing cord through the eyelet for healthcare linen, uniforms and hospitality soft-goods; rivet or bolt-through for canvas tarps, technical covers and heavy coated fabric; cable-tie or carabiner for marine sails, tool-roll bags and outdoor canopies that already carry a lashing eyelet; and a grommet sewn under the lining for leather goods and warranty tabs. In every case the tag re-uses the host's existing eyelet path, so it adds no new piercing and concentrates no new load on the host material.

faq.question: What read range does an RFID eyelet tag deliver, and does HF or UHF suit my application?
faq.answer: An RFID eyelet tag reads at UHF 1-3 m on canvas, fabric and leather, dropping to 0.5-1.5 m with an on-metal spacer against steel container lashings, while the HF variant is a 0-40 mm tap against a phone, POS or laundry-conveyor reader head. Choose UHF 860-960 MHz EPC Gen2v2 for bulk portal and tunnel-wash reads of 50-100 items per cart; choose an HF 13.56 MHz I-CODE SLIX2 or NTAG 424 DNA inlay when the use case is a single deliberate tap — leather-goods authentication, warranty lookup or POS validation — rather than a bulk sweep.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity and lead time for RFID eyelet tags?
faq.answer: MOQ and lead time for RFID eyelet tags are quoted per configuration: the grommet size (Ø 5.0 / 6.35 / 8.0 mm) and alloy, the substrate chemistry (PVC + TPU for industrial laundry, halogen-free TPU for sustainability-audited hosts, or reinforced silicone for marine service), and the chip choice all drive the build, and encode-and-lock services — factory TID left read-only, EPC or NDEF permalocked after WMS / POS encode — are configured per order.
